findings.text: follow-on: the section's done-when states the recheck costs one stat per row, but recheck_worktree_held_rows resolves each worktree-held row through _run_ledger_record, which opens and json-parses the run's per-run file at reckon/hooks/coordinator_obligations.py:906 before the one stat at :966; the cost is one file read and parse plus one stat per row, not one stat, which the dispatcher's resumed instruction sanctioned but which the recorded done-when overstates in the change's favour. No blocking defect found in the change.

item_verdicts.call_sites: no production call site outside the hook: recheck_worktree_held_rows is called only from _prompt and _stop, the two read surfaces the section protects.
item_verdicts.diff: read commit by commit: de60d639 adds recheck_worktree_held_rows and calls it in both hook paths, ab1a7c0c drops the aggregate fallback so the row resolves through the per-run file alone, 2e63acb5 and c694d0ce record the fragment; no third surface offers a worktree-held row (emit at :1125 takes the already-rechecked payload from _stop).
item_verdicts.done_when: the plan's done-when names a read-time check costing one stat per row, a test that promotes a run, keeps the pre-promotion snapshot, invokes the stop hook and asserts no worktree-held row, and the current hook as the negative control that offers it; tests/test_a_worktree_held_row_is_rechecked_at_read.py:309 drives a real crew complete and asserts empty stdout, and the base arm reproduces 3 failed EXIT=1 naming the stale-row cases.
item_verdicts.goal: §21's goal is that the hook rechecks a worktree-held row at read time; reckon/hooks/coordinator_obligations.py:968 recheck_worktree_held_rows filters the live payload in both hook entry points (_prompt at :849 and :865, _stop at :1078), dropping a row whose per-run record shows release.worktree_released true or whose recorded tree is no longer a directory.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; it names base e1e9c9c35 with the new test copied in at 3 failed/47 passed EXIT=1, head ab1a7c0c at 50 passed EXIT=0, and negative_control_log baseline-suite.log; every log path it names exists and each header names the revision quoted and the tree it resolved from.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the diff e1e9c9c35..c694d0ce touches exactly three files, each a declared write path: reckon/hooks/coordinator_obligations.py, tests/test_a_worktree_held_row_is_rechecked_at_read.py, docs/evidence/fragments/the-obligations-hook-reads-a-snapshot/a-worktree-held-row-is-rechecked-at-read.html.

justifications.durability: the aggregate control re-inserting the removed fallback as reachable code fails test_a_row_without_a_per_run_file_is_kept with 'the aggregate ledger was opened' (aggregate-control.log, EXIT=1), so the refusal every case drives under is load-bearing; a regression that reinstates the aggregate read or drops the record check reddens the gate rather than passing silently.
justifications.evidence: tests/test_a_worktree_held_row_is_rechecked_at_read.py:279 drives a real crew complete, captures the snapshot from inside the promotion at the instant the row is still true (:259), and asserts the released row is dropped (:309); the aggregate trap (:194) is asserted armed before each drive so a case cannot pass by installing nothing. I independently reproduced both arms: at base e1e9c9c35 with the new test copied in, 3 failed 2 passed EXIT=1 naming the same three ids, and at head c694d0ce, 40 passed EXIT=0.
justifications.fit: recheck_worktree_held_rows recomputes only count and oldest_age_seconds, mirroring the existing reapply_acknowledgements idiom at reckon/hooks/coordinator_obligations.py:1033; every new symbol names its mechanism (_worktree_row_is_stale, _recorded_tree, _run_ledger_record) and carries no plan, section or ticket label.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/hooks/coordinator_obligations.py:968 drops a worktree-held row where it is offered when reckon/hooks/coordinator_obligations.py:949 finds the run's record reports release.worktree_released or the tree it names is no longer a directory, and both read surfaces (:849, :865, :1078) pass through it, so the stale row the section cites is gone at read time rather than at sweep time. One caveat: the section's done-when states the cost as one stat per row, while the per-run resolution costs one small file read and parse plus one stat per row; the dispatcher's resumed instruction explicitly moved the row off the aggregate, so the goal is met even though the stated per-row cost is a little generous.
justifications.scope_discipline: the diff e1e9c9c35..c694d0ce touches exactly three files, all declared, with 585 insertions and 4 deletions; the declared docs/figures directory was left unused and no change reaches beyond the hook and its test.
